Birinci ayetteki iki sıfat {ar:ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ, tr:er-rahmâni'r-rahîm, gloss:merhameti bol olan, merhamet eden, source:1:1}, ana karnındaki rahimle aynı köktendir. Bu iyilik özellikle zayıfa yönelir: {ar:ورحمة الضعيف والتعطف عليه, tr:ve rahmetü'd-da'îfi ve't-teattufu aleyh, gloss:zayıfa merhamet etmek ve ona şefkatle eğilmek, source:"ر ح م,B001"}. Yeni doğurmuş koyun da bu köktendir: {ar:الشاة الربي التي تحتبس في البيت للبن, tr:eş-şâtü'r-rubbâ, gloss:rubbâ, sütü için evde alıkonan koyundur, source:"ر ب ب,B009"}. Büyütme öğretmeye de uzanır: {ar:العالم المعلم الذي يغذو الناس بصغار العلوم, tr:el-âlimü'l-muallimü'llezî yağzu'n-nâse bi-sığâri'l-ulûm, gloss:insanları önce bilginin küçük parçalarıyla besleyen öğretici âlim, source:"ر ب ب,B003"}. Bu cümle "Rab" ile ikinci ayetteki "âlemîn" kelimesinin kökünü yan yana getirir.

Sure bu görüntüyü bir çerçeve içinde kurar. Birinci ayet rahimle açılır. İkinci ayet büyüten Rabbi anar. Üçüncü ayet, "âlemlerin Rabbi" sözünün hemen ardından iki sıfatı tekrar eder: {ar:ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ, tr:er-rahmâni'r-rahîm, gloss:merhameti bol olan, merhamet eden, source:1:3}. Görüntü ise bu merhametin bir yer ve bir süre içinde işlediğini gösterir: Önce bir ev, sonra halden hale bir büyütme ve sonunda tamamlanma vardır. Altıncı ayet bu evin işlerini ayakta tutanı da hatırlatır: {ar:قوام أهل بيته وقيام أهل بيته؛ الذي يقيم شأنهم, tr:kıvâmü ehli beytihî, gloss:ev halkının işlerini ayakta tutan, source:"ق و م,B004"}. Yedinci ayetteki "en'amte" kelimesinin ailesinde rahat içinde büyütülen çocuklar vardır: {ar:نعم فلان أولاده ترفهم, tr:na''ame fülânün evlâdehû, gloss:falanca çocuklarını bolluk içinde büyüttü, source:"ن ع م,B002"}. Bu iki kelime ayetteki "değil" anlamının yanında, bir evin beslenmesini ve korunmasını duyurur.

Kur'an bu evi açıkça sahneler. strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.32.18	God who gave birth is forgotten	The commentary surrounds nurture with womb and parental care; Moses’ song accuses Israel of forgetting the Rock who gave birth to them, reversing the expected child’s response to the one who formed and raised them.

strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.22.11	cast from the womb toward God	The commentary’s womb image is a home for the child; the psalm says the speaker was cast upon God from birth and relied on God from his mother’s womb, extending the image from maternal shelter to divine care.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.71.6	God supports from the womb	The commentary pictures mercy as care that begins in the womb and continues through a child’s growth; the psalmist says he has leaned on God from birth and was taken from the womb by God.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.127.4	children as fruit of the womb	The commentary begins its frame with the womb as the child’s home; the psalm calls children an inheritance from God and the fruit of the womb a reward, assigning value to the life that grows there.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.131.3	a weaned child with its mother	The commentary describes a child’s growth inside a home and the transition toward completion; the psalm compares its quieted soul to a weaned child beside its mother, where dependence has changed but maternal closeness remains.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.139.14	formed in the mother’s womb	The commentary makes the womb a place where a child grows and is formed; the psalm says God knit the speaker together in his mother’s womb, locating divine making within that home.

strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.11	shepherd carries lambs and leads nursing ewes	The commentary describes the home as a place of protection and sustenance; Isaiah pictures God gathering lambs in his arms, carrying them close, and gently leading nursing mothers.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.66.12	children nursed, carried, and comforted	The commentary links the womb to a child’s home and later nurture; Isaiah depicts Jerusalem’s children nursing, being carried on her hip, and bounced on her knees, giving several concrete stages of maternal care.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:1Sam.2.19	Hannah continues to provide after weaning	The commentary treats nurturing as continuing beyond birth and recognizes care by someone outside the child’s daily home; although Samuel serves at Shiloh, his mother brings him a small robe each year.
strong	tevrat	paralel	WLC:1Kgs.17.23	Elijah returns a son to his mother	The commentary recounts Moses being restored to his mother after separation; Elijah brings the widow’s revived son down and gives him to her, a distinct Hebrew Bible reunion scene.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.21.8	weaning marks a changed stage	The commentary describes raising a child from state to state; Abraham’s feast on the day Isaac is weaned marks the end of nursing and a public transition in the child’s life.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.21.10	a mother and child expelled from home	The commentary presents the home as the child’s place of nurture and protection; Sarah demands Hagar and her son be sent away, showing the contrary case of a household withdrawing that shelter.
strong	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Exod.2.2	Moses hidden before being sent onto the river	The commentary’s Qur’anic account begins with God directing Moses’ mother to nurse him and then place him in the water; Exodus first says she hides the newborn for three months, a distinct step before the basket episode.
strong	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Exod.2.5	Pharaoh’s daughter finds the infant	The commentary says the Pharaoh household takes Moses but emphasizes the sister’s proposal and his return to his mother; Exodus identifies Pharaoh’s daughter as the one who finds the basket and sends her servant to fetch it.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.2.24	kinship made through joined life	The commentary explains “rahim” kinship as relatives who came from one womb; Genesis gives a different foundation for family relation, saying husband and wife become one flesh, adding a bond formed through shared life rather than birth.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.22.6	train a child in a way	The commentary defines tarbiya as bringing a thing through stages toward completion; Proverbs tells an adult to train a child in the way he should go, relating instruction to the child’s later life.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.13.24	discipline as parental care	The commentary portrays raising a child as purposeful formation; Proverbs connects a parent’s love with diligent correction, a sharper form of nurture than the commentary’s gentler household image.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Prov.3.12	q-w-m is not the link; parental discipline is	The commentary defines Rab as raising a child toward completion; Proverbs says the Lord corrects the one he loves as a father corrects a son, supplying a direct Hebrew parental-formation motif.
medium	incil	yorum_gelenegi	SBLGNT:Heb.12.6	Christian reading of Proverbs’ fatherly discipline	The commentary describes nurture as formation toward completion; Hebrews quotes the father-son discipline saying from Proverbs and interprets hardship as the Lord’s treatment of children he receives, giving correction a filial meaning.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.7.11	parents give good gifts to children	The commentary joins mercy with doing good and the Lord with a child’s nurturer; Jesus argues from human parents giving good gifts to their children toward the heavenly Father’s greater generosity.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.5.29	nourishing and cherishing one’s own	The commentary describes a home that nurtures and protects its members; Ephesians says no one hates his own body but nourishes and cherishes it, then uses that care to explain Christ’s care for the church.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.2.11	a father addresses his children	The commentary pairs the mother’s womb and a father’s role in raising a child; Paul recalls exhorting and encouraging each Thessalonian as a father addresses his own children.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.2.12	parental guidance toward a worthy life	The commentary says upbringing leads step by step toward completion; Paul says he urged the community to live worthily of God, like a father guiding children toward their calling.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.11.27	womb and breasts named as maternal blessing	The commentary explicitly develops the womb, the child’s home, and the nurturing relation; a woman blesses the womb that bore Jesus and the breasts that nursed him.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.11.28	Jesus redirects blessing to hearing the word	The commentary connects maternal nurture with the teacher who feeds learners; Jesus answers the womb-and-breast blessing by calling blessed those who hear God’s word and keep it, shifting the measure toward instruction and response.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.19.27	the disciple takes Mary into his home	The commentary describes kinship through a shared womb and care within a household; after entrusting his mother to the disciple, Jesus’ words lead the disciple to take her into his own home, making protection concrete.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Mark.10.16	Jesus takes children in his arms	The commentary says mercy especially bends toward the weak; Jesus takes little children in his arms, lays hands on them, and blesses them after the disciples tried to keep them away.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.1.44	a child moves in the womb	The commentary’s central image is the womb as the child’s home; Elizabeth says the child in her womb leapt when Mary’s greeting reached her, a specific intrauterine scene.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.16.21	labor pain and joy after birth	The commentary recalls pain in the womb after delivery; Jesus compares grief followed by joy to a woman distressed in labor who rejoices after her child is born, preserving the passage’s focus on labor and birth rather than postpartum illness.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.4.5	adoption into God’s family	The commentary notes a spouse raising a child who is not biologically theirs; Paul says Christ redeems those under the law so they may receive adoption as children, applying household adoption to believers.
medium	tevrat	motif	Babylonian Talmud, Kiddushin 29a	father’s concrete duties to a son	The commentary’s Rab raises and teaches a child; Kiddushin lists a father’s obligations to his son, including teaching Torah and a trade, making nurture a set of practical responsibilities.
